Fish and Chips

40 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Par-Frying the Chips

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Cod fillet (skinless)150g300g450g600g
Potatoes (for chips)200g400g600g800g
Plain flour (for batter)60g120g180g240g
Cornflour20g40g60g80g
Baking powder½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground turmericpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Cold beer (or sparkling water)100ml200ml300ml400ml
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Vegetable oil (for frying)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Dried marrowfat peas (for mushy peas)75g150g225g300g
Butter (for mushy peas)5g10g15g20g
Mint (chopped)pinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Sugar (for mushy peas)¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Malt vinegar (to serve)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Lemon wedge1234

Steps

  1. Soak the dried marrowfat peas in cold water overnight (or use a quick-soak method following the packet). Drain before cooking.
  2. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick chip shapes. Rinse under cold water to wash off extra starch, then pat dry with a clean towel.
  3. Ask an adult to help heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to about 130°C — this first fry cooks the chips through without browning them yet. Fry the chips for 5–6 minutes until soft but pale, then lift them out and let them drain and cool.
  4. In a bowl, whisk together the plain flour, cornflour, baking powder, turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Slowly pour in the cold beer, whisking as you go, until you have a smooth, lump-free batter about as thick as double cream. Turmeric is what gives fish and chip shop batter its golden color.
  5. Turn the oil up to about 180°C. Dip each piece of cod into the batter, letting the extra drip off, then carefully lower it into the hot oil.
  6. Fry the fish for 5–6 minutes, turning once, until the batter is deep golden and crisp and the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Lift out and drain on paper towels.
  7. Turn the oil back up to 190°C and fry the part-cooked chips a second time for 2–3 minutes, until golden and crunchy on the outside. Drain and sprinkle with a little extra salt.
  8. While the chips fry, warm the drained marrowfat peas in a small pot with a splash of water, the butter, chopped mint, and sugar. Mash roughly with a fork until thick and a little chunky — this is 'mushy peas.'
  9. Serve the fish and chips together with a scoop of mushy peas, a lemon wedge, and malt vinegar on the side for splashing over everything.

Shepherd's Pie

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Buttery Mashed Potato Topping

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Lamb mince150g300g450g600g
Onion (diced)40g80g120g160g
Carrot (diced)30g60g90g120g
Celery stalk (diced)¼½¾1
Garlic (cloves)1234
Tomato purée½ tbsp1 tbsp1½ tbsp2 tbsp
Worcestershire sauce1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Lamb or beef stock100ml200ml300ml400ml
Plain flour (to thicken)1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Frozen peas30g60g90g120g
Dried thyme¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Oil (for browning)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Potatoes (for mash)200g400g600g800g
Butter (for mash)15g30g45g60g
Milk (for mash)30ml60ml90ml120ml

Steps

  1. Peel the potatoes, cut into even chunks, and put them in a pot of cold salted water. Ask an adult to help bring it to a boil, then simmer 15–18 minutes until a fork slides in easily.
  2. While the potatoes cook, heat a splash of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until softened.
  3. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add the lamb mince, breaking it up with a spatula, and cook 5–6 minutes until no pink remains.
  4. Sprinkle the flour over the mince and stir for 1 minute so it coats everything.
  5. Stir in the tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce, stock, and thyme. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened like a rich gravy.
  6. Stir in the frozen peas and season with the salt and black pepper. Spoon the mince into a baking dish and spread it level.
  7. Drain the cooked potatoes and mash them with the butter and milk until smooth and fluffy. Season with a little more salt if needed.
  8. Spoon the mash over the mince in an even layer, then run a fork over the top in swirls — this helps the peaks turn golden and crisp in the oven.
  9. Ask an adult to help bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Browning the Sausages

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pork sausages2468
Potatoes (for mash)200g400g600g800g
Butter (for mash)15g30g45g60g
Milk (for mash)30ml60ml90ml120ml
Onion (sliced)½11½2
Plain flour (for gravy)1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Beef stock150ml300ml450ml600ml
Worcestershire sauce1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Oil (for frying)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp

Steps

  1. Peel the potatoes, cut into chunks, and boil in salted water 15–18 minutes until fork-tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk until smooth. Season with a little salt and keep warm.
  2. While the potatoes cook, heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the sausages and cook, turning every couple of minutes, for 12–15 minutes total until browned all over and cooked through with no pink in the middle. Lift out and set aside, keeping warm.
  3. Using the same pan, add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden.
  4. Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for 1 minute so it soaks up the fat.
  5. Slowly pour in the beef stock, stirring constantly to smooth out any lumps. Add the Worcestershire sauce and season with black pepper.
  6. Simmer the gravy 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
  7. Pile the mash onto plates, lean the sausages against it, and pour the onion gravy generously over the top.

Chicken Tikka Masala

45 min (+ marinade)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Simmering the Masala Sauce

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thigh (boneless)150g300g450g600g
Plain yogurt (for marinade)40g80g120g160g
Lemon juice1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Garlic (cloves, grated)1234
Fresh ginger (grated)½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Garam masala½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Butter or ghee10g20g30g40g
Onion (diced)40g80g120g160g
Ground cumin½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground coriander½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Tomato passata100g200g300g400g
Double cream40ml80ml120ml160ml
Oil (for cooking chicken)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Fresh cilantro (to garnish)small handfulsmall handfulhandfulhandful
Basmati rice (dry, to serve)60g120g180g240g

Steps

  1. In a bowl, mix the yogurt, lemon juice, half the garlic and ginger, half the garam masala, the turmeric, chili powder, and a pinch of salt. Add the chicken pieces and turn to coat evenly. Cover and marinate in the fridge at least 30 minutes.
  2. Ask an adult to help heat a splash of oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer and cook 3–4 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink inside. Lift out and set aside.
  3. In the same pan, melt the butter or ghee over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft and golden.
  4. Add the remaining garlic and ginger, the cumin, coriander, and remaining garam masala. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
  5. Pour in the tomato passata and simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and turns a deep red-orange.
  6. Stir in the double cream and return the cooked chicken to the pan. Simmer 3–4 minutes so the chicken warms through and soaks up the sauce.
  7. Taste and add a little more salt if needed. Scatter with fresh cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

Steak and Ale Pie

1 hr 45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Braising the Beef Filling

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Braising beef (chuck), cubed150g300g450g600g
Plain flour (to coat beef)1 tbsp2 tbsp3 tbsp4 tbsp
Onion (diced)40g80g120g160g
Carrot (diced)30g60g90g120g
Garlic (cloves)1234
Brown ale or stout100ml200ml300ml400ml
Beef stock150ml300ml450ml600ml
Tomato purée½ tbsp1 tbsp1½ tbsp2 tbsp
Worcestershire sauce1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Bay leaf1122
Fresh thyme¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Oil (for browning)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Ready-rolled puff pastry¼ sheet½ sheet¾ sheet1 sheet
Egg (beaten, for egg wash)1122

Steps

  1. Toss the beef cubes in the flour with a pinch of salt and pepper until lightly coated. Ask an adult to help heat a splash of oil in a large, heavy pot over high heat.
  2. Brown the beef in batches, 2–3 minutes per batch, until deep brown on the outside. Set the beef aside.
  3. Add a little more oil if needed, then add the onion and carrot. Cook 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds more.
  4. Return the beef to the pot. Pour in the ale, scraping up any browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon.
  5. Add the beef stock, tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf, and thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer.
  6. Turn the heat down low, cover with a lid slightly ajar, and let it simmer gently for 1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is fork-tender and the sauce has thickened. Remove the bay leaf and taste, adjusting salt and pepper.
  7. Spoon the cooled filling into a pie dish. Roll the puff pastry out a little bigger than the dish and lay it over the top, trimming the excess and crimping the edges with a fork to seal.
  8. Cut a small slit in the center of the pastry to let steam escape, then brush the top all over with the beaten egg.
  9. Ask an adult to help bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25–30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden brown.

Toad in the Hole

40 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Yorkshire Pudding Batter Rising

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pork sausages2468
Plain flour60g120g180g240g
Eggs1234
Milk100ml200ml300ml400ml
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Vegetable oil or beef dripping (for the tin)1 tbsp2 tbsp3 tbsp4 tbsp
Onion (sliced, for gravy)½11½2
Plain flour (for gravy)1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Beef stock (for gravy)150ml300ml450ml600ml
Worcestershire sauce (for gravy)1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Butter or oil (for gravy)10g20g30g40g

Steps

  1. Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl until you have a smooth, lump-free batter about the thickness of pouring cream. Let it rest at room temperature for 20–30 minutes.
  2. Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pour the oil or dripping into a metal roasting tin and put it in the oven for 8–10 minutes until it's smoking hot.
  3. While the tin heats, brown the sausages in a separate frying pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes, turning them, just until golden on the outside.
  4. Carefully take the very hot tin out of the oven. Quickly place the browned sausages in the tin, then immediately pour the batter around them and slide it straight back into the oven.
  5. Bake 25–30 minutes without opening the oven door until the batter is puffed up dramatically and deep golden brown.
  6. While it bakes, make the gravy: melt the butter or oil in a small pan over medium-low heat, add the sliced onion, and cook 8–10 minutes until soft and golden.
  7. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then slowly pour in the beef stock, stirring to smooth out lumps. Add the Worcestershire sauce and simmer 4–5 minutes until thickened.
  8. Cut the toad in the hole into portions right away and serve immediately with the onion gravy poured over.

Sunday Roast Chicken with Roast Vegetables

1 hr 30 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Chicken Before Roasting

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken (bone-in, skin-on pieces)400g800g1.2kg1.6kg
Butter (for the chicken)10g20g30g40g
Lemon¼½¾1
Garlic (cloves)1234
Fresh thymefew sprigsfew sprigssmall bunchsmall bunch
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Potatoes (for roasting)150g300g450g600g
Carrots75g150g225g300g
Parsnips75g150g225g300g
Oil (for the vegetables)as neededas neededas neededas needed
Plain flour (for gravy)1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Chicken stock (for gravy)100ml200ml300ml400ml

Steps

  1. Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Pat the chicken pieces dry with a paper towel.
  2. Rub the chicken all over with the butter, then season generously with salt and pepper. Tuck the garlic cloves, lemon quarters, and thyme sprigs around the chicken in a roasting tin.
  3. Peel the potatoes, carrots, and parsnips and cut into even chunks. Toss them in a separate roasting tin with a splash of oil and a pinch of salt.
  4. Put both tins in the oven. Roast the chicken for about 45–55 minutes, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear with no pink when you cut into the thickest part.
  5. Add the vegetable tin to the oven partway through (about 35–40 minutes before the chicken finishes), turning the vegetables once halfway, until they're golden and a fork slides in easily.
  6. Once the chicken is done, lift it onto a plate to rest for 10 minutes. Keep the roasting tin with all the flavorful juices and bits.
  7. Place the roasting tin over medium heat on the stove (ask an adult to help). Sprinkle in the flour and stir into the juices for 1 minute to make a paste.
  8. Slowly pour in the chicken stock, stirring and scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the tin, and simmer 3–4 minutes until it thickens into a gravy. Taste and season if needed.
  9. Carve the rested chicken and serve with the roast vegetables and gravy poured over the top.

Sticky Toffee Pudding (Bonus)

45 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Whisking the Toffee Sauce

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pitted dates (chopped)75g150g225g300g
Bicarbonate of soda¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Boiling water90ml180ml270ml360ml
Butter (softened, for sponge)25g50g75g100g
Dark brown sugar (for sponge)40g80g120g160g
Eggs1234
Self-raising flour60g120g180g240g
Vanilla extract (for sponge)¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Butter (for toffee sauce)25g50g75g100g
Dark brown sugar (for toffee sauce)40g80g120g160g
Double cream60ml120ml180ml240ml
Salt (for toffee sauce)pinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp

Steps

  1. Put the chopped dates and bicarbonate of soda in a heatproof bowl. Ask an adult to help pour the boiling water over them, then let the mixture sit for 10 minutes.
  2. Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a baking dish with a little butter.
  3. In a separate bowl, beat the softened butter and dark brown sugar together until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract.
  4. Fold in the self-raising flour gently until just combined.
  5. Pour in the date mixture (including all the soaking liquid) and fold together gently until you have a smooth, fairly runny batter.
  6. Pour the batter into the prepared dish and bake 30–35 minutes until risen and a skewer poked into the center comes out clean.
  7. While it bakes, make the toffee sauce: melt the butter and dark brown sugar together in a small pot over medium-low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
  8. Pour in the double cream and a pinch of salt, and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until it turns a rich, glossy toffee color and coats the back of a spoon.
  9. Poke a few holes in the warm sponge with a skewer and pour about a third of the warm toffee sauce over the top so it soaks in. Serve slices with the extra sauce poured over.
